subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me a 6-mark exam-style question on {lo} for {board} {level} {subject}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Two angles lie on a straight line. One is 110°. What is the other?
questions.explain: Angles on a straight line sum to 180°, so 180° − 110° = 70°.

questions.q: What is the size of each exterior angle of a regular hexagon?
questions.explain: Exterior angles sum to 360°, so each is 360° ÷ 6 = 60°.

questions.q: The bearing of B from A is 070°. What is the bearing of A from B?
Co-interior (allied) angles between parallel lines: one is 130°. What is the other?
Two angles in a triangle are 55° and 65°. What is the third angle?
questions.explain: Angles in a triangle sum to 180°, so 180° − 55° − 65° = 60°.

questions.q: Two angles are vertically opposite. One is 47°. What is the other?
questions.explain: Vertically opposite angles are equal, so it is 47°.

questions.q: What is the sum of the interior angles of a pentagon?
Three angles meet at a point and are 120°, 150° and x. What is x?
questions.explain: Angles around a point sum to 360°, so x = 360° − 120° − 150° = 90°.

questions.q: An isosceles triangle has an apex angle of 40°. What is each base angle?
questions.explain: The two equal base angles share 180° − 40° = 140°, so each is 70°.

questions.q: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
questions.explain: A square has 4 lines of symmetry.
